espn-603997.headline: Twenty months apart, Dupont and Ntamack pick up in Lyon
beats: Antoine Dupont and Romain Ntamack start together at half-back for the first time since March 2025. France put 42 on Australia and 42 on Japan in July without either: Dupont missed the whole tour with a calf issue.
Fiji bring Nathan Hughes, a former England international making his Test debut for them, in Jake White's second game in charge. The last England side Fiji saw scored 73 against them at home in July.
Fiji lost 34–21 in France last November. Win this time, by any margin, and France drop below England in the world rankings.
South Africa come to France the following Friday. That gives the reunited pair one evening to remember how it works before somebody tests the "soft underbelly".

espn-603998.headline: One coach has his bosses' backing, one squad a pay row
beats: Steve Borthwick goes into Sunday with the full support of his bosses, and his players have denied rumours of a rift. Australia arrive embroiled in a pay row.
Ugo Monye thinks the siege suits England: "they tend to perform when their backs are against the wall." His worry is the ill discipline that has plagued them of late.
England have won two straight since their worst-ever Six Nations, and beat Australia 25–7 at Twickenham last November. Australia have since conceded 50 and 43 to New Zealand in a fortnight.
Win, though, and Australia take England's fifth place in the world rankings, dropping them below Scotland as well. A result is the best argument either side could bring to the table.

England have been backed into a corner – it should bring out their best against Australia | Ugo Monye

espn-603999.headline: A France win hands New Zealand the world No. 1 spot
beats: South Africa have been first in the world since 31 August. Lose at the Stade de France by any margin and they drop to second, behind New Zealand, the side they beat in three of four Tests in August and September.

France were beaten 17–32 at home on 8 November 2025. Their year since has been loud at both ends: 42 points against both Australia and Japan in July, after conceding 50 to Scotland and 46 to England in March.

South Africa's last game before November was a 38–42 defeat in Australia, so this is not an unbreakable side. Victor Matfield expects Rassie Erasmus to use his uncapped youngsters, Yaqeen Ahmed among them, in exactly this kind of game, and says he "doesn't mind giving those players an opportunity."
South Africa then go to Ireland a week later. New Zealand, level with them on 20 Championship points, can follow both results from a distance.

sources.title: Springboks legend: Don't be surprised if Rassie Erasmus backs bolters against France and Ireland

espn-604000.headline: Italy's last win was England. Argentina are next
beats: Italy sit last of twelve on zero points, with four defeats and a points difference of minus 153. That win over England, 23–18 in Rome, was in March.
Argentina are hardly arriving in form. They lost 42–12 in Dublin on 6 November, with Ireland scoring six of the eight tries amid a stream of forward disruptions. They have won once all year.
Win, and Italy climb to ninth in the world, above Fiji and Wales.
Fiji come to Italy a week later, also on zero points. That leaves Italy two chances to stop being the answer to who is bottom.

sources.title: Argentina Crash against Ireland amid Endless Forward Disruptions
Ireland player ratings: Back three shine in Pumas rout

espn-604001.headline: New Zealand scored 52 on their last trip to Cardiff
beats: Wales scored 26 that day, on 22 November 2025, and still lost by 26. Their most recent result before this November was a 43–0 loss in South Africa in July, without a try.

New Zealand have since put 50 and 43 past Australia in October, seven tries each time. They are level on points with South Africa at the top of the Nations Championship, and first meets second on finals weekend.

Steve Tandy has framed this month as pivotal, with Japan, New Zealand and Australia all coming to Cardiff, and says his side must kick on faster. A win would lift Wales above Fiji to ninth in the world.
Australia arrive a week later, having conceded 93 to New Zealand in their last two Tests.

espn-604002.headline: England have lost to Italy this year. Japan are next.
beats: That 18–23 defeat in March came in what became England's worst-ever Six Nations. A week later they lost 46–48 in France.

They have since won twice, 73–8 in Fiji and 31–24 in Argentina, with 16 tries between them. Japan beat Fiji 20–15 in September and lost to them 28–34 in October, and have slid from ninth to 12th in the rankings since.

Steve Borthwick has his bosses' full support. He also has a newspaper report of player unrest over his leadership, which Jamie George says left the squad "really upset". Lose here and England drop to seventh in the world, below Scotland and Australia.
New Zealand come to London a week later. That is not the week to be explaining Japan.

espn-604003.headline: Ireland can only lose ground before South Africa visit
beats: Ireland have been third in the world since July, and anything short of a win here drops them below France. South Africa, unbeaten at the top of the Nations Championship, come to Ireland next.

Ireland ran in six tries past Argentina, three of them for Hugo Keenan, and Andy Farrell still wanted more ruthlessness. Fiji conceded 73 to England in July and have no points from three Nations Championship games.
They did win last time out, 34–28 away to Japan, with four tries.
Joey Carbery's last Ireland cap, his 38th, came against Fiji in 2022. His way back runs through Fiji A, in Cork on 20 November.

espn-604004.headline: Sixth plays seventh, and the gap is a rounding error
beats: Scotland are sixth in the world and Australia seventh, with less than half a point between them. They swapped those places on 19 October, and an Australian win by any margin swaps them back.

Australia arrive having conceded 50 and 43 to New Zealand in October, with a pay row running alongside. Scotland scored seven tries against both Argentina and France this year and still let in 38 and 40.
Win and Scotland climb to fifth, above England, before Japan come to Murrayfield. They are already level with England on points in the Nations Championship.

The fixture turns 100 next year. Australia have won 22 of the 35 meetings, including 16 straight after Scotland won in Brisbane in 1982. Gregor Townsend once spent a summer playing club rugby in Sydney. The affection should last until kickoff.

espn-604005.headline: Beating New Zealand by 14 again would not be enough
beats: England beat New Zealand 33–19 at Allianz Stadium on 15 November 2025. Only a win by 16 or more, two points better than that, lifts England to third in the world, above Ireland and France.

England's Six Nations included an 18–23 defeat by Italy in March, part of what Planet Rugby called their worst-ever Six Nations campaign. Since then they have put 73 on Fiji and beaten Argentina 31–24.

New Zealand lost three in a row to South Africa, then scored seven tries in each of two wins over Australia, 50–19 and 43–21. They are unbeaten in the Nations Championship and level on points with South Africa at the top.
Sixteen points is a lot to find against a side that put 93 on Australia in a week.

espn-604006.headline: Jack Dempsey gets an early look at his new address
beats: Jack Dempsey says a move to Japan will keep him fresh and hungry through the long build-up to next year's World Cup. Now the Scotland No 8's side get Japan at Murrayfield.

He also says Scotland can be the best and worst team in the world. Their year agrees: 50–40 over France at home, then beaten 43–21 by Ireland a week later. They have conceded 38 or more in four of their last five.

Japan have their own split personality. They beat Fiji 20–15 in September, then lost to them 34–28 at home in October, and slid from 9th to 12th in the world. Win in Edinburgh and they are straight back up to 9th.
Either way, Dempsey's new hosts will have an opinion on the result.

espn-604007.headline: Porter has had a year to think about that scrum
beats: Andrew Porter has not played for Ireland since South Africa won 24–13 in Dublin on 22 November 2025. That night South Africa won six penalties from 16 scrums, one of them a penalty try, and Porter was one of four Irish players yellow-carded.
Calf problems then kept him out of the Six Nations and the summer tour, which left plenty of time to replay it. James Tracy, his former Leinster front-row colleague, called the scrum "obliterated".

Ireland come in off a 42–12 win over Argentina, six tries and three of them for Hugo Keenan. Andy Farrell still wants them "a little bit more ruthless". South Africa have just beaten Italy 66–7 in Turin, a month and a half after losing 42–38 to Australia.
Win, and Ireland push South Africa down to second in the world, below New Zealand. It will probably be settled where it went wrong last year, at the scrum.

espn-604008.headline: Two winless sides in Udine; at most one stays so
beats: Italy are bottom of the Nations Championship after four games. Fiji sit one place above them after three. Neither has a point, and Italy's last win was 23–18 over England in March.
Italy conceded 47 in New Zealand and 57 in Australia on consecutive July weekends. Fiji come in having beaten Japan 34–28 away on 24 October, a month after losing to them 20–15.
Fiji are also two places higher in the world rankings, though not by much: an Italy win in Udine puts Italy ninth, directly above them.
Neither side plays again until the World Cup, so whoever loses carries it into 2027.
